newsitem.title: EGYPT: EGYPT TO SELL REMAINING STAKE IN CEMENT FIRM.
newsitem.headline: EGYPT TO SELL REMAINING STAKE IN CEMENT FIRM.

text.p: Egypt will sell its remaining stake in Amriyah Cement to investors through the stock exchange and via global depository receipts (GDRs), a government newspaper said on Wednesday.
The sale of 48 percent of Amriyah's total equity currently owned by the state's Holding Company for Metallurgical Industries is part of the Egyptian government's privatisation programme.

Al-Ahram newspaper quoted Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif as saying the ministerial committee on privatisation on Tuesday approved the sale of 20 percent of the holding company's stake in Amriyah through the bourse and 28 percent via GDRs. The paper gave no further details.
"The sale will encourage investors. There's been foreign interest in Amriyah for a long time now which is probably why the government decided to issue GDRs," said Mona Ibrahim of Prime Investment.
"Amriyah is efficient and I'm sure the GDRs will be covered immediately," she added.
Amriyah made net pre-tax profits of 129.254 million pounds ($38 million) for the first nine months of financial year 1996/7.

The Amriyah GDR offering will be the second for a cement firm and the country's fifth. The others were for Suez Cement, Misr International Bank/MIBANK, Commercial International Bank CIB, and privatised al-Ahram Beverages, also known Pyramids Beverages,.
The holding company lowered its stake in Amriyah Cement to 48 percent in January when it completed the sale of 3.4 million shares in the firm.
On Tuesday, Amriyah shares closed up 0.08 pounds at 79.8 after trade in more than two million pounds.
